With the first notes while sitting in the theater, I looked up the soundtrack on Apple Music and saved it. I could tell instantly it was something special.
That 5 piano note medley in part 1  is so effective, feels like longing and love, and nostalgic…just a lot of feels from that.

The first part of Love Is In The Air is so sad after having watched the movie. Because that one plays when everything is still innocent and Nikki still has a chance to be saved before she starts her downward spiral. In fact, in those early days it might have been possible for Bear to trick her into undoing his wish by snapping a willow so she would have her autonomy back. It just turned so dark and miserable by part 2 of the song; two insane minds swimming in tainted love.

The part from 0:41 to 0:49 especially gets me. That bit sounds like the faint remains of a hollow longing for the past when he hadn't made the wish yet. It's like it's emphasizing the sadness and hopelessness of her losing her autonomy, making the real Nikki sound like a distant lost memory and mourning her even though she's still in there, but mixed with the shy sweetness of her confession of liking him. Sad to us because we know she's already suffering behind a mask and we know how it's going to end, even if now seems okay, so the music is almost foretelling the upcoming montage and saying "Bear, you might as well just have that and enjoy it while you can. Get what you wished for, before it all turns to hell, because we know you can't or won't save her." It's one of the parts that brings the tears for me.

And the second part when she's too far gone, and she's wished Bear into that same spiral, they act so innocent right before that kiss, like two young teenagers who have a crush on each other about to try their first kiss. A tiny sweet moment of mutual insane romance after so much murder and trauma that it took just to get there. And despite all that struggle, it will only last for a few seconds before he dies, and she stands there smiling with real love at the man's heart she has finally conquered and claimed, having no idea she's going to lose him forever AGAIN. And then stop existing herself, leaving behind the shell shocked mind to take over the body again and suffer all the consequences.

At 2:49, that part right there is yet _another_ one that keeps bringing me to tears, where the background bass tone changes again along with the strings lowering a bit. That part of the music feels like an environmental transition from one place to another, just like how the camera changes right before it to show them both from the side, and Bear appears approaching at 2:49 with the music transition. Like it's emphasizing introducing Freaky Bear to Freaky Nikki for the first time and it's beautiful, it shows only them and none of the carnage in that beautiful moment with the kiss, and again that feeling of "we've lost everything and everyone we cared about but we still have each other. This is the end, nothing else exists except for us," is profound in that moment. Even though they're both trapped, I feel deeply for both Freaky Bear and Freaky Nikki, two people who didn't ask to be here but at least have one beautiful thing to enjoy, which is each other.

The first part of Love Is In The Air is so sad after having watched the movie. Because that one plays when everything is still innocent and Nikki still has a chance to be saved before she starts her downward spiral. In fact, in those early days it might have been possible for Bear to trick her into undoing his wish by snapping a willow so she would have her autonomy back. It just turned so dark and miserable by part 2 of the song; two insane minds swimming in tainted love.

The part from 0:41 to 0:49 especially gets me. That bit sounds like the faint remains of a hollow longing for the past when he hadn't made the wish yet. It's like it's emphasizing the sadness and hopelessness of her losing her autonomy, making the real Nikki sound like a distant lost memory and mourning her even though she's still in there, but mixed with the shy sweetness of her confession of liking him. Sad to us because we know she's already suffering behind a mask and we know how it's going to end, even if now seems okay, so the music is almost foretelling the upcoming montage and saying "Bear, you might as well just have that and enjoy it while you can. Get what you wished for, before it all turns to hell, because we know you can't or won't save her." It's one of the parts that brings the tears for me.

And the second part when she's too far gone, and she's wished Bear into that same spiral, they act so innocent right before that kiss, like two young teenagers who have a crush on each other about to try their first kiss. A tiny sweet moment of mutual insane romance after so much murder and trauma that it took just to get there. And despite all that struggle, it will only last for a few seconds before he dies, and she stands there smiling with real love at the man's heart she has finally conquered and claimed, having no idea she's going to lose him forever AGAIN. And then stop existing herself, leaving behind the shell shocked mind to take over the body again and suffer all the consequences.

At 2:49, that part right there is yet _another_ one that keeps bringing me to tears, where the background bass tone changes again along with the strings lowering a bit. That part of the music feels like an environmental transition from one place to another, just like how the camera changes right before it to show them both from the side, and Bear appears approaching at 2:49 with the music transition. Like it's emphasizing introducing Freaky Bear to Freaky Nikki for the first time and it's beautiful, it shows only them and none of the carnage in that beautiful moment with the kiss, and again that feeling of "we've lost everything and everyone we cared about but we still have each other. This is the end, nothing else exists except for us," is profound in that moment. Even though they're both trapped, I feel deeply for both Freaky Bear and Freaky Nikki, two people who didn't ask to be here but at least have one beautiful thing to enjoy, which is each other.
